card.statement:
The graded $k[\hbar]$ -algebra

(2.13)

$R_{Kah}:=k[z^{\alpha}]\otimes\mathrm{Sym}H^{2}_{T\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X)$

is the Kähler ring of differential operators, where $z^{\alpha}$ is the formal variable of degree $0$ indexed by $\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\Sigma_{Kah,+}$ , subject to the relation

(2.14)

$xz^{\alpha}=z^{\alpha}(x+\hbar\langle\alpha,\bar{x}\rangle),$

where $\bar{x}\in H^{2}(X)$ denotes the image of $x\in H^{2}_{T\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X)$ under the projection map in the cohomology exact sequence.

Similar to the definition of $R_{eq,reg}$ , by inverting $(1-z^{\alpha})$ for $\alpha\in\Sigma_{Kah,+}$ , we obtain $R_{Kah,reg}$ .

The quantum $D$ -module is defined using the equivariant quantum cohomology of $X$ , whose definition in the present form depends on assuming Conjecture 2.20.
card.label: Definition 2.26

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
